what_its_for: Milnacipran is used to treat fibromyalgia, a condition that causes widespread muscle pain, tenderness, and fatigue. It works by balancing certain natural chemicals in your brain (serotonin and norepinephrine) that affect how your body senses pain.
how_to_take: Take milnacipran by mouth with or without food. Taking it with food may help reduce nausea, especially when you first start. Swallow the tablet whole. Try to take it at the same times every day to keep a steady amount in your body. Do not suddenly stop taking this medicine without talking to your doctor first, as stopping too quickly can cause dizziness, nausea, or other uncomfortable feelings.
dosing: Your doctor will usually start you on a low dose and slowly increase it over the first two weeks. The typical starting dose is 12.5 mg once on the first day, then 12.5 mg twice daily for days 2 to 3, then 25 mg twice daily for days 4 to 7, and finally the usual maintenance dose of 50 mg twice daily. Some patients may be increased to 100 mg twice daily. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions, as your dose may be different.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store milnacipran at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medications out of reach of children and pets. Dispose of unused or expired medication safely — ask your pharmacist about a drug take-back program near you.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking milnacipran, as it can increase the risk of liver problems and may worsen side effects like dizziness. Do not take MAO inhibitors (such as phenelzine, tranylcypromine, selegiline, or linezolid) within 14 days of taking milnacipran, as this combination can cause a serious, life-threatening reaction. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery until you know how this medicine affects you, since it can cause dizziness or blurred vision. Tell your doctor about all other medications, vitamins, and supplements you take, especially blood thinners, other antidepressants, migraine medicines, or pain relievers like aspirin or ibuprofen.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: thoughts of suicide or self-harm, unusual changes in mood or behavior, high fever, fast heartbeat, or stiff muscles (signs of serotonin syndrome), chest pain or shortness of breath, painful or difficult urination, severe headache or blurred vision (possible sign of high blood pressure), unusual bleeding or bruising, signs of liver problems such as yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, or severe stomach pain, or seizures. Also call your doctor if you feel more anxious, agitated, or restless, especially in the first few weeks of treatment.
when_it_works: Some patients may notice small improvements in pain or energy within the first 1 to 2 weeks, but it may take 4 to 8 weeks of regular use to feel the full benefit. Be patient and keep taking your medication as prescribed, even if you do not notice changes right away. Do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor.
special_populations: Older adults (65 and over): Use with caution, as older adults may be more sensitive to side effects such as dizziness, falls, and changes in blood pressure. Your doctor may start you on a lower dose. Kidney problems: If you have severe kidney disease, your dose will likely need to be reduced. Tell your doctor about any kidney problems. Liver problems: Use caution if you have liver disease. Milnacipran is not recommended for people with severe liver problems. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Talk to your doctor before using this medicine if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Taking it late in pregnancy may cause withdrawal symptoms in your newborn. Children: Milnacipran is not approved for use in anyone under 18 years of age.
